title: Stage Actress Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure, Detective Takagi, guest legendary detective Heihachiro Shiota) omitted by convention even though Shiota drives the on-screen deduction. No event nodes: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved, sharing an order integer. Unusually rich in red herrings: Kogoro Mouri himself publicly (and wrongly) accuses Yuichi Uda first; Eiko Nakayama is briefly suspected via the water pitcher (which turns out clean, since the cyanide was in the glass); and props man Junichi Tateoka is a genuine secondary culprit for a *different* crime (the threat letter and a curtain-rigging attempt to injure Shoko) who is not the poisoner. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Marks on Hitomi Sasaki's hands match forcibly detaching a taut fishing line, consistent with reeling the poisoned weight back up in a hurry.
The fishing line used in the murder is still in Sasaki's pocket after everyone present is ordered to stay exactly where they were -- she never had a chance to dispose of it.

Pen-imprint indentations on a backstage writing pad match the wording of the threat letter, identifying Tateoka as its author -- a real, separate crime uncovered mid-investigation that is not the murder.

Cyanide kills almost instantly, yet Shoko drank water normally after swallowing a prop capsule earlier and the rehearsal ran uninterrupted for 40 minutes -- rules out any method that introduces the poison significantly before she actually drank, and rules out the pitcher (clean) in favor of something added directly to her glass moments before.
